subject: Follow-up: RCA & escalation comparison vs. hyperscalers — next tests and ask
thread_text:
From: Karim Singh <k.singh@omniretail.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Rao <priya.rao@consult-ops.com>
Date: Sun, 20 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial call — escalation expectations and incident comparatives

Thanks for the call this morning, Aditya. Useful context. Two quick asks from our side as we prep the eval team: 1) Can you provide a succinct comparison of how Redwood handles incidents and RCAs vs what we should expect from hyperscalers (AWS/GCP) — specifically time-to-RCA, support SLA tiers, and what RCA contents look like? 2) We want a short checklist of tests to validate vendor incident response during our trial window (what to trigger, what logs to request).

Karim
Head of Site Reliability — OmniRetail

----
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Karim Singh <k.singh@omniretail.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 08:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial call — escalation expectations and incident comparatives

Karim — thanks for the clear asks. Drafting a short packet for you and the SRE team; attaching a concise RCA comparison PDF and a CSV runbook checklist for trial tests. High level summary below, followed by proposed next tests and timelines.

High level compare (TL;DR):
- Time-to-RCA: Redwood aims for preliminary RCA notes within 48 hours for P1 (initial timeline + mitigation summary) and a full stitched RCA within 7 business days for complex infra/model issues. Hyperscalers often provide preliminary incident summaries within 24–72 hours but their RCA cadence is tied to platform-level ops + account engineering; multi-tenant noise can delay model-specific root cause artifacts.
- Support SLA tiers: Redwood offers a Sales + Dedicated SLA path: P1 on Dedicated customers = 1 hour response, P1 on Hosted customers = 4 hour response (with escalation options). Hyperscalers' public SLA focuses on platform availability (VMs, networking)—detailed support response depends on account tier and AE involvement.
- RCA contents: Redwood RCAs include: timeline, request traces (token-level latency traces if requested), model variant state, KV cache snapshots where relevant, GPU job metadata, mitigation steps and patch plan, retrospective mitigations. Hyperscaler RCAs emphasize infra components (host/network/storage) and will sometimes route model-level findings back to the model vendor.

Proposed trial tests (what to trigger + what to collect):
1) Controlled P1: Simulate an AWS AZ flake to test cross-region failover and time-to-failover + fallback routing; collect route decision logs and latency histograms.
2) Model degradation: Push a crafted prompt set that increases sequence length and KV pressure to observe queuing/backpressure and per-token latency; collect GPU utilization, batch sizes, and KV cache hit rates.
3) Cold-start regression: Re-deploy model variant and hit with steady load to measure cold-start latency distributions and warm-up token performance.
4) auth/logging audit: Request redwood audit logs for API key usage and confirm KMS/HSM access logs for Private deployment.

Next steps: 1) I’ll loop in Marissa to outline the trial contract + proposed SLA. 2) Neha will provide the runbook CSV with exact log fields to request. 3) We can run the first controlled test next week if you confirm timing.

Best,
Aditya Rao
Senior Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference

Attachments: 20270620-omniretail-rca-comparison.pdf (summary), runbook-support-sla-table.csv (fields)

----
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Karim Singh <k.singh@omniretail.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 10:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial call — escalation expectations and incident comparatives

Karim — quick commercial note on SLAs and trial governance: for the Proof-of-Value (POV) we can include a temporary elevated support tier (no-cost) that mirrors our Dedicated SLA for the duration of the 4-week trial: P1 phone escalation + 1 hour response objective. For production Dedicated seats we’ll need a reserved capacity commitment. I’ll send a redline-friendly mutual action plan after Karim confirms the go-ahead on test dates.

A couple of clarifications on Aditya’s tests: for test #2 (model degradation) we should plan a canary traffic bucket and explicit throttles so your prod-calls aren’t impacted. Also recommend including a runbook step to capture raw token traces (redacted keys) so we can reconstruct latency per-request.

-M
Marissa Cole
Account Executive — Redwood Inference

----
From: Karim Singh <k.singh@omniretail.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Rao <priya.rao@consult-ops.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial call — escalation expectations and incident comparatives

Thanks Marissa — that makes sense. Couple quick questions before we lock dates: 1) Can you confirm Redwood will provide token-level traces (anonymized) for the model degradation test? 2) If we do trigger a P1 during the POV, what does the escalation path look like (who is on call, and how do we evidence response SLAs)? Also, how do your RCAs handle multi-tenant noise — will the RCA explicitly state whether a noisy neighbor was the cause?

Regards,
Karim

----
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Karim Singh <k.singh@omniretail.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2027 09:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial call — escalation expectations and incident comparatives

Karim — short answers: 1) Yes, we can provide token-level traces for POV tests; traces will be anonymized and delivered as trace files (we redact payloads and keys). 2) Escalation path for elevated POV support: Level 1 (onsite Support Engineer) — immediate triage; Level 2 (Inferencing SRE) — deep diagnostic; Level 3 (Platform Engineering + Model Ops) — fixes and RCA. For P1 during the POV we will log the incident in our internal incident tracker and provide time-stamped acknowledgements (via email + PagerDuty webhook) — those artifacts are part of the RCA packet. 3) On multi-tenant noise: our RCAs include correlation analysis to separate infra-level signals (node/host/network) from model-level signals (KV cache, batching). If noisy neighbor contributed, we include evidence (host CPU/IO spikes, tenant token streams) and recommended mitigations (isolate on Dedicated pool or increase isolation settings).

Neha Kapoor
Head of Product Operations — Redwood Inference

----
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Karim Singh <k.singh@omniretail.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, AWS Sales <aws-sales@amazon.com>
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2027 16:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial call — escalation expectations and incident comparatives

Karim — attaching the two files Marissa/Neha referenced. Quick concrete asks to lock the POV: 1) Confirm test window: preferred 28–30 Jun (three-day window) or flag alternative dates. 2) Confirm canary traffic plan and whether OmniRetail can provide a dedicated test API key for tracing (recommended). 3) Please confirm the person who will own incident coordination on your side (name + PagerDuty contact).

If you’re okay, we’ll also reach out to the AWS account team (cc’d) to request any infra-level logs we may need when we run the controlled AZ flake test; that usually speeds correlation.

Thanks — looking forward to finalizing the plan.

-Aditya
